title: record — one session's handoff
description:
The session record shed drafts on every Stop and finalizes at SessionEnd. SETTLED once finalized (`draft: false`, `ended_at` set): immutable, provenance-carrying, the cross-session record. Its prospective parts — `open_threads`, `watch_outs`, an `intent` — are leased artifacts nested inside it (thread.json, intent.json); the record itself never expires.

EVERY FIELD DECLARES ITS EMISSION SCOPE — `x-scope: shared | private`. This annotation IS the private layer's allowlist: shed.py derives FIELD_SCOPE from this file at import and `split_record` projects the draft into the shared archive (`handoff/sessions/<ended>__<sid8>.json`, committed, mirrored) and the private record (`handoff/private/<sid8>.json`, gitignored, this machine only). Anything a person SAID is private: `human_first`, `human_last`, `session_topic` (a whitespace-normalized copy of her first sentence — the same words) and the transcript pointer. A key not declared here reaches neither file. `--share <field>` on finalize is the contracted emission that lets one private field into one shared record, and `shared_fields` records that it happened. The record never crosses the git boundary by replication, only by a scope this schema declares (project_contracted_emission_invariant, at field granularity).

Every field also declares who stands behind it — `x-tier`, tier.json's enum: the human's sentences are `authored`; what shed computes from git and the transcript is `derived` and carries a `basis` reading per instrument (basis.json) so a missing transcript is BLIND, never 'zero turns'; `tldr` and the gated lists are `interpreted` unless an entry says otherwise. Record-level tier is stated in the schema rather than repeated on every record because it is a property of the writer, not of the instance.

The archive shape is the one hololoom_mcp already reads (its /handoff skill writes a superset — `summary`, `active_threads`, `capkip`, `briefs` — and shed stands down when such an archive exists for the session). This schema is shed's contract: what shed writes, every key declared. Readers stay lenient; the writer is strict.

sid8.description: First 8 of the session id (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID); `nosid` when none was available. Identity of the record is the filename stem `<ended>__<sid8>`, never the sid8 alone — a sid8 spans several archives when a session resumes.

source.description: Which writer produced the record: `shed` here. finalize stands down when a non-shed archive for the sid8 already exists — the richer record always wins; shed is the backstop.

draft.description: true while the record is the Stop hook's live draft under handoff/drafts/; false once finalized.

started_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC. The transcript's first timestamp, or the first draft's time; kept across refreshes.

ended_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC at finalize; null on a draft.

intent.description: What the session declared before it touched files, copied verbatim from the live scratchpad. Absent when nothing was declared (ABSENT = no probe, not no intent).

tldr.description: One sentence readable outside the project. Mechanically the first sentence of the last assistant turn — model prose even when clipped, so interpreted. The extractiveness number is computed over it.

summary.description: Shed's own statement of how the record was made and what each field means — a fixed text, so a reader of the bare file knows `empty` means unknown, not none.

turns.description: Text turns read from the transcript. 0 with basis[transcript].state = BLIND means the transcript could not be read, not that nothing was said.

progress.description: Commit subjects since `started_at` (`git log --format='%h %s'`), oldest last as git prints them. Derived from git; basis[git] says whether git could be read.

open_threads.description: Polarity `open`. Empty means unknown, not none. Filled by a human or a model; every entry passes the evidence gate at finalize.

decisions.description: Settled choices worth carrying. Same gate.

files_touched.description: Union of paths in commits since `started_at` and paths dirty at draft time, sorted. Paths only — a filename is a pointer, never content.

first_commit_seconds.description: Seconds from `started_at` to the session's first commit; null when there was none. One of the arc's two coordination-cost numbers (the other is est_tokens to orient, in metrics.jsonl).

extractiveness.description: Share of the record's interpreted word 3-grams found in the transcript turns and commit subjects, 0.0–1.0; null when there was too little interpreted text. Falling across sessions is the drift alarm. Written at finalize only.

basis.description: One reading per instrument shed drafted from — `transcript` and `git`. The rider that keeps `turns: 0` and `progress: []` from being read as silence when the instrument was BLIND.

shared_fields.description: Private fields that crossed into THIS shared record by `--share`, sorted. Empty on the hook path, which never shares. The record of a contracted emission, on the record.

private_sha256.description: Commit-and-reveal: sha256 of the private record's canonical JSON (the private fields only, sorted keys), carried on the shared file next to nothing else from them. `shed.py verify <archive>` checks this machine's private record against it, and a `--share`d sentence is checkable by anyone holding the shared file. The git boundary is the seal; this is the journal at level zero.

session_topic.description: First user turn, first sentence, whitespace-normalized, capped. PRIVATE: it is her sentence in other whitespace, and a shared topic that is her sentence is the leak the layer exists to close.

human_first.description: The human's first sentence, byte-for-byte, never regenerated. PRIVATE by default; orient reads it back on the machine that recorded it and prints it before tldr, so her words frame the synthesis and not the reverse.

human_last.description: The human's last sentence, byte-for-byte. PRIVATE. `--share human_last` is the worked example of a contracted emission.

transcript_path.description: Where the transcript was read from. PRIVATE: a pointer into ~/.claude/projects is a pointer to every word of the session.
